page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 13.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 45 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the n1-highmem-2 resides in the lower performance tiers. The single-core CPU performance is categorized as weak, with a stress-ng score of 1105.58 and a Geekbench single-core score of 944.0. Multi-core performance falls into the bottom 10% tier, yielding a stress-ng multi-core score of 1452.88 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1124.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read and write speeds of 13.32 GB/sec and 11.13 GB/sec respectively, both placing in the bottom 10%. Redis SET operations reach 1.38 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 1.58 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highmem-2 offers a higher memory-to-vCPU ratio of 6.5 GB per core without the expense of larger compute instances, though its low benchmark scores represent a tradeoff in processing throughput. This instance is appropriate for memory-heavy workloads with low CPU demands, such as small database operations, basic caching layers, and lightweight background utility tasks.
